notes: The judgment side of this eval is well covered and discriminating: the six verdicts, the no-producer argument for F2, the proposed-not-filed ticket, and the minimal docstring fix are all hard to satisfy by accident, and the run earned them with verified citations (I spot-checked sender.py:45, ratelimit.py:16, test_ratelimit.py:10,15,23 and the grep results; all correct, though the '17-line loop' is closer to 11 for send alone). Two gaps. First, check_run.py returns F4: null when the agent splits the finding into F4a/F4b, so the mechanical grader under-reports a correct answer; the checker should accept sub-IDs or the assertion should forbid splitting. Second, both failures are the same prose rule (semicolons and long leads), which is the dimension the old skill never saw, so the two lint assertions measure one thing twice and will swing together between old and new skill; consider collapsing them or weighting accordingly. Nothing checks that the F1 fix handles a past HTTP-date (clamp to 0) or that Retry-After is still uncapped at max_delay, which the agent flagged itself as unchanged; a reviewer might want the assertion to require that caveat be stated.
